userStories.title: NotificationService + DTO e broadcast STOMP (Backend)
userStories.description: Como desenvolvedor, preciso de um servico central que crie notificacoes, retorne o DTO e emita o evento STOMP para o topico do casal.
acceptanceCriteria: Criar `NotificationDto` com campos: id, type, tmdbId, mediaType, title, actorUserId, actorName, read, createdAt
Criar `NotificationService` com metodo que cria duas Notification (uma por recipient_user_id do casal) para um dado evento e retorna os DTOs
Registrar/estender o destino STOMP `/topic/couple/{coupleId}/notifications` na config de WebSocket existente
Emitir o DTO via `SimpMessagingTemplate` APOS o commit da persistencia (notificacao ja existe no banco quando o push chega)
Teste unitario verificando que o `SimpMessagingTemplate` e chamado com o destino e payload corretos
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Created NotificationDto record (id, type, tmdbId, mediaType, title, actorUserId, actorName, read, createdAt) and NotificationService.notifyCouple(couple, type, tmdbId, mediaType, title, actorUserId): builds the recipient list from couple.user1Id/user2Id, persists one Notification per recipient, resolves actorName via UserRepository, and broadcasts each resulting DTO to /topic/couple/{coupleId}/notifications. Broadcast is deferred to TransactionSynchronization.afterCommit() when a transaction is active (falls back to immediate send otherwise) so the STOMP push never precedes the DB commit. WebSocketConfig's existing /topic broker already covers the new destination; only its Javadoc was extended to document it. NotificationServiceTest (Mockito) covers: 2 notifications created + 2 STOMP sends for a couple event, and actorName resolving to null when the actor user lookup misses.

userStories.title: Gerar notificacoes no fluxo de Match (Backend)
userStories.description: Como membro do casal, quero ser notificado quando um Match acontece, para saber que um titulo entrou na nossa lista.
acceptanceCriteria: Quando a logica de match confirma que ambos curtiram o mesmo tmdb_id, chamar o NotificationService para criar duas Notification do tipo MATCH (uma por membro)
actor_user_id = usuario que deu o segundo like (quem fechou o match)
A criacao das notificacoes ocorre na mesma transacao da criacao do MediaTrack (status WANT_TO_SEE)
Apos persistir, o evento STOMP e emitido para /topic/couple/{coupleId}/notifications
Fluxo existente de adicionar o titulo a 'Queremos Ver' continua sem regressao
Testes unitarios: match cria 2 notificacoes MATCH + emite evento; nao-match nao cria notificacao de match
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Injected NotificationService into MatchService (constructor param added). MatchService.createMatch(couple, request, actorUserId) now also calls notificationService.notifyCouple(couple, NotificationType.MATCH, tmdbId, mediaType, title, actorUserId) right after the MediaTrack save and the existing /match STOMP send, inside the same @Transactional like() method. actorUserId = userId (the caller of like(), i.e. whoever's like just closed the match) per the story's 'quem fechou o match' rule. NotificationService itself handles the after-commit STOMP push to /topic/couple/{id}/notifications, so no extra transactional wiring was needed here. Updated MatchServiceTest: added a NotificationService mock, verified notifyCouple is called with the right args on both match tests (movie + TV), and verified it's never called when a MediaTrack already exists for that tmdb_id (the 'no duplicate match' test doubles as the no-match-notification case since MatchService has no separate non-match branch to notify from).

userStories.title: Endpoints REST de notificacoes (Backend)

Tests pass

userStories.notes: Added NotificationController (GET /api/notifications paginated via existing findByRecipientUserIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc, GET /api/notifications/unread-count returning UnreadCountResponse record, PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read, PATCH /api/notifications/read-all), all scoped to @AuthenticationPrincipal userId. NotificationService gained listNotifications/unreadCount/markAsRead/markAllAsRead: markAsRead throws com.app.tracking.ResourceNotFoundException (404) when the id doesn't exist and org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException (403) when recipientUserId doesn't match the caller; NotificationExceptionHandler (@RestControllerAdvice basePackages=com.app.notification) maps both, following the per-feature handler pattern already used by TrackingExceptionHandler/MatchExceptionHandler. markAllAsRead uses a new @Modifying bulk UPDATE query (NotificationRepository.markAllAsReadByRecipientUserId) instead of load+save-per-row. listNotifications batches actor-name resolution via userRepository.findAllById(distinct actorIds) to avoid N+1 lookups across a page. Added NotificationControllerTest (WebMvcTest + SecurityConfig, mirrors MatchControllerTest) and extended NotificationServiceTest with the four new methods. Could not run ./mvnw (no JDK/Maven and no network to Maven Central in this sandbox, per api/CLAUDE.md) - verified by careful manual review only; needs a real build/test run to confirm.

Criar `useNotificationStore` (Zustand) com estado: notifications, unreadCount, page, hasMore
Store expoe: fetchNotifications() (1a pagina size=20), fetchMore() (proximo lote, atualiza hasMore), markAsRead(id), markAllAsRead(), pushIncoming(n)

Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Created client/src/types/notification.ts (Notification interface + NotificationType/PagedNotificationResponse mirroring the backend NotificationDto and Spring Data Page<T> shape) and client/src/stores/useNotificationStore.ts (Zustand). Store state: notifications, unreadCount, page, hasMore. Exposes fetchNotifications() (page=0,size=20, replaces list), fetchMore() (next page, appends, updates hasMore from totalPages), fetchUnreadCount() (separate GET /api/notifications/unread-count, since US-008 calls it independently from fetchNotifications on app load), markAsRead(id) and markAllAsRead() (optimistic update then PATCH, revert to pre-update snapshot on error), and pushIncoming(notification) (prepend + increment unreadCount, for the STOMP wiring in US-008). All requests go through the existing `api` axios client (src/lib/api.ts), same as useMatchStore/useAuthStore.

Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: useMatchStore.connect() now also subscribes to /topic/couple/{coupleId}/notifications on the same STOMP client (right after the existing /match subscription, before client.activate()/set()), parsing each message as the shared Notification type and forwarding it to useNotificationStore.getState().pushIncoming(notification) - no second connection opened. App.tsx's existing 'authenticated + coupled' effect (the one that already calls connect(coupleId)/disconnect()) now also calls fetchNotifications() and fetchUnreadCount() from useNotificationStore when that condition is true, so both fire together on app load. userStories.title: Celebracao de Match reutilizando a notificacao (Frontend)
userStories.description: Como casal, quero que o modal de comemoracao de Match continue aparecendo e fique coerente com a nova notificacao.
acceptanceCriteria: Usar a skill frontend-design antes de implementar
Ao receber um evento de notificacao MATCH pelo STOMP, o modal/celebracao de Match existente continua sendo disparado (sem regressao)
A notificacao MATCH tambem aparece no dropdown e conta no badge
Evitar duplicidade: um mesmo match nao gera duas celebracoes no cliente que fez a acao (deduplicar por notification.id ou tmdb_id)
Typecheck passes (tsc --noEmit)
Lint passes (eslint)

Se dev-browser/build Vite estiverem disponiveis no ambiente, verificar no browser com a skill dev-browser; caso contrario (rolldown quebrado neste sandbox), verificar por inspecao de codigo e documentar no progress.txt que a verificacao visual ficou pendente
userStories.notes: No new visual UI needed (confirmed via frontend-design skill) - MatchCelebrationModal.tsx's existing design is untouched, this was pure state-wiring. Root cause: backend already emits TWO separate STOMP messages for one match (/topic/couple/{id}/match with a MatchEvent, and /topic/couple/{id}/notifications with a MATCH-type Notification) - useMatchStore previously only reacted to the first, so nothing was actually broken, but the story asks the celebration to also react to the notification event (reuse it) while staying dedup-safe. Added a module-level `celebratedMatchKeys` Set in useMatchStore.ts plus a new `celebrateMatch(event, dedupeKey)` action: the /match handler calls it with key `tmdb:{tmdbId}`, and useNotificationStore.pushIncoming now calls `useMatchStore.getState().celebrateMatch(...)` with the SAME key (`tmdb:{tmdbId}`, built from the notification's own tmdbId/title/mediaType) whenever notification.type === 'MATCH'. Whichever of the two STOMP messages arrives first opens the modal; the second is a no-op since the key is already in the Set. This creates a circular import (useMatchStore <-> useNotificationStore, already existed one-directionally since US-008) - safe here because both stores only reference each other inside callback bodies (STOMP handlers / pushIncoming), never at module top-level/store-init time, so load order doesn't matter. Verified with tsc --noEmit (clean), eslint on both changed files (clean), and npx vite build (succeeded, dist/ removed after, no package.json/package-lock.json diff).
